details: The European Central Bank (ECB) and other EU central banks have recommended revising the MiCA regulations to drop the requirement for stablecoin issuers to hold a minimum proportion of their reserves as bank deposits. They argue this could expose lenders to runs on stablecoins and less stable deposits, proposing instead that reserves be held in assets maturing within one to five working days. This move aims to prevent stablecoins from altering bank funding structures.
title: ECB Suggests Loosening Stablecoin Deposit Rules

details: The European Central Bank has initiated "Pontes," a service to connect its payment infrastructure with distributed-ledger markets, enabling banks and investors to settle eligible tokenized transactions using central-bank euros. This wholesale initiative, separate from the proposed retail digital euro, demonstrates increasing institutional recognition of distributed ledgers as practical settlement technology. Deutsche Bank, Santander, and Clearstream are among the first institutions to be onboarded.
title: ECB Launches Blockchain Settlement Service 'Pontes'

details: A recent Wall Street Journal report indicates that major global economies are proving surprisingly resilient to sustained higher central-bank interest rates and multi-decade-high bond yields. Economists are reportedly increasing their neutral-rate estimates, with the Federal Reserve's median now at 3.25% and the eurozone's top end near 2.5%. This resilience, partly supported by AI investment, could alter the macroeconomic outlook for crypto and potentially support adoption and fundraising.
sourceName: The Coin Republic (citing Wall Street Journal)
title: Global Economies Resilient to Higher Interest Rates

details: As of September 17, 2026, El Salvador's national Bitcoin holdings have reached 7,777 BTC, with a floating profit of $162 million. This increase occurs despite a 2024 IMF agreement that restricted public sector Bitcoin purchases. The country has reportedly continued to expand its reserves through private donations and wallet consolidations, as noted in the 2026 IMF review, indicating an active strategy despite external constraints.
title: El Salvador Continues Bitcoin Accumulation Despite IMF Agreement

details: Bitcoin experienced a dip, trading around $84,000, following a rise in US 10-year government bond yields to 5.11%—a level last seen during the 2007 financial crisis. This, combined with escalating geopolitical concerns in the Middle East and hawkish statements from Fed officials signaling potential further rate hikes, has led to a risk-off sentiment in the market. Historically, spikes in bond yields initially prompt investors to favor assured returns on Treasuries over crypto assets.
title: Bitcoin Dips Amid Rising Bond Yields and Geopolitical Tensions
